messages.content:
How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a step‑by‑step guide on how to **generate a RESTful API request** for the *“Get information of device connector versions”* API in Cisco Nexus Dashboard (v6.3.1). The instructions assume you already have a Nexus Dashboard instance up and running and that you have the necessary credentials (admin or a role that can read device‑connector data). --- ## 1. Locate the API in the Dashboard UI | Step | Action | Screenshot (optional) | |------|--------|------------------------| | 1 | Log in to the Nexus Dashboard web UI. | | | 2 | From the left‑hand navigation, click **API Explorer** (or **Developer Tools → API Explorer**). | | | 3 | In the API Explorer, use the search box or the “Device Connector” category to find the API named **“Get information of device connector versions”**. | | > **Tip:** If you’re not sure of the exact name, look for an endpoint that contains `/device-connector/versions` or similar. --- ## 2. Inspect the API definition Once you click the API, you’ll see a detailed view that includes: | Section | What you’ll see | |---------|-----------------| | **Method** | `GET` | | **Endpoint** | `/api/v1/device-connector/versions` (may vary slightly – check the UI) | | **Query Parameters** | e.g. `?limit=100&offset=0` (optional) | | **Headers** | `Authorization: Bearer `
`Accept: application/json` | | **Response Schema** | JSON object with fields such as `connectorId`, `version`, `status`, `releaseDate`, etc. | --- ## 3. Generate the request ### 3.1 Using the UI “Generate Request” button 1. Click the **Generate Request** button (usually located at the top right of the API detail pane). 2. The UI will display a ready‑to‑copy request in the format you selected (e.g., **cURL**, **Python**, **JavaScript**, **Postman**). 3. Copy the snippet. > **Example (cURL)** > ```bash > curl -X GET "https:///api/v1/device-connector/versions" \ > -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ > -H "Accept: application/json" > ``` ### 3.2 Using the “Run” button If you want to test the request immediately: 1. Click **Run**. 2. The response will appear in the **Response** tab. 3. You can view the raw JSON, status code, headers, and timing. --- ## 4. Authentication – obtaining an access token The Nexus Dashboard uses OAuth2 bearer tokens. If you don’t already have a token: 1. **Login** via the UI or via a separate OAuth endpoint. 2. **Request a token** (e.g., using the `/oauth/token` endpoint). ```bash curl -X POST "https:///oauth/token" \ -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \ -d "grant_type=password&username=&password=&client_id=" ``` 3. Extract the `access_token` from the JSON response and paste it into the `Authorization` header. > **Note:** Some deployments use **Basic Auth** instead. In that case replace the `Authorization` header with `Basic `. --- ## 5. Example end‑to‑end request ```bash # 1. Get an access token (replace placeholders) TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST "https://nexus-dashboard.example.com/oauth/token" \ -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \ -d "grant_type=password&username=admin&password=admin123&client_id=dashboard-client" | jq -r .access_token) # 2. Call the Device Connector Versions API curl -s -X GET "https://nexus-dashboard.example.com/api/v1/device-connector/versions" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ -H "Accept: application/json" | jq . ``` > **Output (sample)** > ```json > { > "total": 3, > "items": [ > { > "connectorId": "dc-01", > "version": "1.2.3", > "status": "active", > "releaseDate": "2024-07-15" > }, > ... > ] > } > ``` --- ## 6. Exporting the request for other tools In the API Explorer, you can also: - **Export** the request as a **Postman collection** or **OpenAPI spec**. - **Copy** the raw HTTP request (headers + body). - **Generate** code snippets in multiple languages (Python, Java, Go, etc.). --- ## 7. Troubleshooting | Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix | |---------|--------------|-----| | 401 Unauthorized | Token expired or missing | Refresh token or re‑authenticate | | 404 Not Found | Wrong endpoint path | Verify the exact path in the API Explorer | | 400 Bad Request | Invalid query parameters | Check required/optional params | | 500 Internal Server Error | Backend issue | Check Nexus Dashboard logs or contact support | --- ### Quick Reference | Item | Value (example) | |------|-----------------| | Base URL | `https://nexus-dashboard.example.com` | | Endpoint | `/api/v1/device-connector/versions` | | Method | `GET` | | Headers | `Authorization: Bearer `
`Accept: application/json` | | Query Params | `limit`, `offset` (optional) | | Response | JSON array of connector versions | --- **That’s it!** You now know how to generate, test, and use the “Get information of device connector versions” API in Cisco Nexus Dashboard v6.3.1. If you run into any specific errors or need help with a particular query parameter, feel free to ask!
